Task: Develop a complete lesson plan for teaching probability to high-school students.

High-School Probability Lesson Plan  
Duration: 1 class period (≈ 55 minutes)  
Grade level: 9 – 10 (can be adapted up or down)

1. Learning Objectives  
• Define probability as the long-run relative frequency of an event.  
• Distinguish between theoretical and experimental probability.  
• Calculate probabilities of single events and simple compound events (independent & mutually exclusive).  
• Represent probabilities with fractions, decimals and percentages.  
• Interpret probability values to make informed predictions.

2. Standards Alignment (examples—adapt to your jurisdiction)  
• CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.HSS.CP.A.1-5 (Conditional Probability & Rules of Probability)  
• Next Generation Science Practice: Analyzing & Interpreting Data  

3. Materials & Technology  
• Decks of cards (½ deck per pair)  
• 1 coin and 1 six-sided die per student  
• Probability spinners printed on card stock or digital spinner website  
• Whiteboard or smartboard  
• Student handout (guided notes + practice)  
• Exit ticket slips  
• Optional: Desmos/GeoGebra applet for empirical probability simulation

4. Anticipatory Set (5 min)  
Teacher flips a coin 10 times in front of class, tallying heads/tails. Ask: “What do you predict will happen next flip? Why?” Display class predictions, segue into probability language.

5. Direct Instruction & Guided Notes (10 min)  
• Definition: P(Event)= (# favorable outcomes)/(# total equally likely outcomes).  
• Range 0 – 1; 0 → impossible, 1 → certain, 0.5 → equally likely.  
• Theoretical vs. experimental examples (coin vs. our actual 10 flips).  
• Mutually exclusive events: P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B).  
• Independent events: P(A and B)=P(A)·P(B).

6. Guided Practice Stations (24 min, 6 min each × 4)  
Students rotate in pairs; record findings on handout.

Station A – Coins  
• Predict and then flip 20 times; compute experimental P(Heads). Compare to 0.5.

Station B – Dice  
• Roll two dice 30 times; tally sums. Compute experimental P(sum = 7). Show theoretical 6/36.

Station C – Card Draw  
• From shuffled half-deck (26 cards), calculate theoretical P(red), P(face card), P(red OR face). Check by drawing 20 replacement draws.

Station D – Spinner  
• Use 4-section spinner (⅛,¼,⅜,⅜ sizes). Spin 30 times; compare distribution to theoretical fractions.

Teacher circulates, poses guiding questions, checks calculations.

7. Whole-Class Debrief (8 min)  
• Groups share discrepancies between theoretical & experimental results.  
• Discuss Law of Large Numbers; emphasize difference between short-run variation & long-run stability.  
• Quick mini-lecture on common misconceptions (e.g., Gambler’s Fallacy).

8. Independent Practice (Homework or last 5 min)  
Worksheet with:  
a) Word problems on simple probability.  
b) Tree diagram for independent events (e.g., coin then die).  
c) Challenge: Conditional probability of drawing 2 aces without replacement.

9. Assessment  
Formative: station observations, guided-practice calculations.  
Exit Ticket (last 3 min): “Bag has 5 blue, 3 green, 2 red marbles. a) P(red) ? b) P(blue or green) ? c) After replacing, what is P(red then green) ?” Collect on way out.

10. Differentiation & Supports  
• Provide color-coded fraction strips for visual learners.  
• Offer calculator use for arithmetic to focus on reasoning.  
• Extension: Have advanced students derive formula for P(at least one head in 3 flips).  
• Scaffolded sentence starters for ELLs: “The probability of ___ is ___ because ___.”

11. Reflection (for teacher, post-lesson)  
• Which station caused most misconceptions?  
• Did exit tickets show mastery ≥ 80 %? If not, plan reteach/spiral review.  
• Note timing adjustments for next period.

12. Safety & Classroom Management  
• Clear rotation paths, timer projected for station changes.  
• Stress respectful handling of shared materials.  

13. Resources  
• NCTM Illuminations probability activities  
• PhET “Plinko” simulation  
• Khan Academy “Intro to Probability” videos (for flipped prep or remediation)

End of Lesson Plan
